tagline: Indian Creek, rolling farms and a valley beside Peters Mountain.
intro: Farm Heritage Road crosses Monroe County on two-lane state and U.S. highways, moving from Indian Creek’s winding course to rolling farm plateaus and the Sweet Springs Valley beside Peters Mountain. The Federal Highway Administration gives the route’s length as 59.45 miles and allows approximately 1.5 hours for the drive. The state byways guide presents it as a view of agricultural communities retaining the character of earlier generations. The guide links the survival of old houses, farms and public buildings to the limited reach of industry and commercial development in this part of the state.

The road received its byway designation in June 1996. Travel had already helped shape the country it crosses: stagecoach lines carried settlers across the Alleghenies through Union, while nearby mineral-spring resorts helped the region grow. Union retains buildings from the years before the Civil War, when the resort economy flourished.

Peterstown stands beside the Virginia border. Indian Creek and its covered bridge precede Union, the county seat. East of Union, WV 3 reaches Gap Mills before Sweet Springs, where it meets WV 311. The final landscape is the Sweet Springs Valley beneath the ridge of Peters Mountain.

moments.title: Peterstown
moments.text: A diamond discovery gives this border town an unexpected place in the county’s story. In 1928, Grover C. Jones and his son William, known as Punch, found the 34.48-carat Jones Diamond here. Peterstown takes its name from settler Christian Peters and lies on the Virginia line, directly across Rich Creek from Midway in Giles County.

moments.title: Indian Creek Covered Bridge
moments.text: Ray and Oscar Weikel built this small covered crossing in 1898. It measures 49.25 feet long and 11.5 feet wide, near US 219 in Monroe County. The Monroe County Historical Society owns the bridge, which entered the National Register in 1975. Hoke Brothers Construction of Union restored it in 2000.

moments.title: Union
moments.text: Union’s courthouse came after the county itself. When Monroe County’s first court met in 1799, the town did not yet exist; James Alexander subsequently offered twenty-five acres, including a courthouse lot. By 1810, a courthouse and jail occupied its center. The present courthouse dates from 1881 and uses the Romanesque style. Other buildings survive from the earlier resort economy, when mineral springs and stagecoach travel helped Union grow. The historic district entered the National Register in 1990. The Monroe County Historical Society preserves the Caperton Law Office, Owen Neel House and Old Baptist Church among its historic properties in town.
